method_definition: Expected frozen-current-belief MBD + relaxed RPCBF inside each forecast; full online POAM + RPCBF in execution
belief_evaluation: Direct full POAM predictive model and its existing coherent Matheron sampler; no lookup-table belief approximation
decisions: Two independent nominal reference-acceleration coordinates per decision interval; all coordinates optimized by original MBD, with a separate reverse chain per start. The original PD reference tracker and current-mean air-force compensation run before RPCBF. Coarse graph trajectories initialize only.
coarse_initialization: Online clarity-guided 64x37 graph, compiled Dijkstra, distinct free-space destinations and temporary cuts across geometrically discovered bottlenecks to retain distinct alternative passages. Approximate sensing ranking only; the full objective scores all candidates.
initialization: Untrained zero-mean POAM prior, plus one actual noisy observation at the initial position. No prior survey or supplied true field.
objective: Expected time integral of equal-area whole-free-space mean(max(target-q,0)), plus the old study clearance and speed terms: max(0.06-clearance,0)^2 + 2*max(speed-3.1,0)^2 while alive. The clearance preference uses this environment safety margin, not the larger historical environment threshold. Predicted contact stops motion and sensing; the full remaining-horizon decay cost is retained. Executed monitoring deficit is reported separately from planning penalties. No uncertainty bonus, tail selection, arrival reward, or injected dwell schedule.
limitations: Finite Monte Carlo and diffusion budget; optimizer convergence is not established.
Existing POAM spectral residual sampling and finite inducing representation are retained, not replaced.
Forecast safety is evaluated every 0.2 s; actual RPCBF every 0.05 s. Both use 0.01 s RK4 physics.
Relaxed RPCBF permits constraint slack; finite-sample filtering is not a global safety guarantee.
Existing CFD is provisional; this is one paired development seed per environment.
